---
name: neurico-host-local-llm-fallback
description: "On the shared /data neurico host, API keys may be absent; GPUs are shared/contended; vLLM recipe, cached models, and pitfalls (pkill self-kill, cudnn clash, prompt_logprobs OOM)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: e7324b18-29e9-4db0-ae5a-a9f0cd196a49
  modified: 2026-10-16T18:23:14.513Z
---

Observed 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-16 in neurico research workspaces on this host:
- OPENROUTER_KEY / OPENAI keys were NOT set in the session env (`~/.flamebird/neurico/.env` has it commented out). Resource-finder stage may be skipped (no papers/, datasets/, code/).
- Local models + datasets cached in `/data/transformers/hub` (HF_HOME=/data/transformers): Qwen2.5-{0.5,1.5,3,7,14}B-Instruct safetensors, Qwen3/3.5 family, Llama-3.1-8B, GGUFs; datasets incl. glue(sst2 only), stanfordnlp/sst2, samsum, ag_news, boolq, mmlu. huggingface.co is reachable for extra downloads (curl resolve/main URLs).
- 2026-10-16: 4x RTX A6000 (48GB) present but shared — other users' jobs held ~42GB on 3 GPUs and intermittently grabbed the 4th. Approach that worked: vLLM 0.31 (`uv add "vllm>=0.10"`; unpinned `uv add vllm` resolved an ancient 0.4 build), small `gpu_memory_utilization` (~0.11 ≈ 5GB) for ≤1.5B models on the leftover slices, plus a bash wrapper that polls `nvidia-smi` free memory and retries launch. vLLM checks free mem ≥ util×total at startup.
- 2026-10-14 (no GPU then): llama.cpp multi-server CPU fallback worked; `transformers` CPU generation much slower.
- Pitfalls: `pkill -f <pattern>` inside a Bash call whose text contains the pattern kills the calling shell (find PIDs, kill by PID separately). Leftover `nvidia-cudnn-cu12` 8.x from a failed install breaks flashinfer ("Found 2 libcudnn.so.x") — `uv pip uninstall nvidia-cudnn-cu12`. vLLM `prompt_logprobs` materialises full-vocab logits → OOM on small slices; cap `max_num_batched_tokens` (~1024). Don't edit a bash script while a running loop is executing it.
- Label-restricted log-probs in vLLM: `logprobs_mode="processed_logprobs"` + `allowed_token_ids=label_ids` returns log-softmax renormalised over the labels.

Update 2026-10-16 (inter-model-agreement workspace): 4×A6000 present but shared — other neurico sessions keep each GPU at ~6–10 GB free, fluctuating second to second. What worked:
- `uv venv --python 3.12` (default 3.14 breaks vLLM); pyproject needs `requires-python="==3.12.*"` and `[tool.uv] package=false`.
- vLLM 0.31: no bitsandbytes; set `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` (JIT build fails); `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`.
- Use pre-quantized 4-bit AWQ/GPTQ checkpoints (~5.5 GB for 8B): Qwen/*-AWQ, hugging-quants Llama-3.1/gemma-2 AWQ-INT4, tiiuae/Falcon3-7B-Instruct-AWQ, solidrust Mistral AWQ, kaitchup Olmo-3/Phi-3 GPTQ.
- Cap gpu_memory_utilization to ~12.5 GB and retry on startup OOM via a scheduler loop; max_model_len 2560, max_num_seqs 64.
- Gated models in /data/transformers/hub (meta-llama Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, google/gemma-7b-it) have weights but no config/tokenizer → unusable; unsloth mirror of Llama-3.1 is complete. Disk /data is ~100% full.

Update 2026-10-16 (few-shot-ordering workspace, 2nd session): a "Begin research execution" prompt can land on a workspace where a prior session already finished most work (REPORT.md exists, background jobs killed at session end). Check logs/*.status and REPORT first and resume only the interrupted pieces rather than restarting. Monitor `tail -n0 -F` on status files missed an append; poll status files directly instead. Qwen2.5-14B bf16 (~30 GB) won't fit when GPUs have ≤23 GB free.

Update 2026-10-16 (system_prompt_residual_effects workspace): the neurico runner can kill a session at its 6h limit (return_code 143) and relaunch with the same prompt while detached background jobs (e.g. `run_all.sh`) keep running. On start, check for existing planning.md/REPORT.md, `*_PLACEHOLDER` markers, `.neurico/pipeline_*.json`, `*.partial` checkpoints and live PIDs before redoing anything; usually you only need to wait for the jobs and re-run the scoring/analysis.

---
name: neurico-host-local-llm-fallback
description: "On the shared /data neurico host, API keys may be absent; GPUs are shared/contended; vLLM recipe, cached models, and pitfalls (pkill self-kill, cudnn clash, prompt_logprobs OOM)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: e7324b18-29e9-4db0-ae5a-a9f0cd196a49
  modified: 2026-10-16T18:23:14.513Z
---

Observed 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-16 in neurico research workspaces on this host:
- OPENROUTER_KEY / OPENAI keys were NOT set in the session env (`~/.flamebird/neurico/.env` has it commented out). Resource-finder stage may be skipped (no papers/, datasets/, code/).
- Local models + datasets cached in `/data/transformers/hub` (HF_HOME=/data/transformers): Qwen2.5-{0.5,1.5,3,7,14}B-Instruct safetensors, Qwen3/3.5 family, Llama-3.1-8B, GGUFs; datasets incl. glue(sst2 only), stanfordnlp/sst2, samsum, ag_news, boolq, mmlu. huggingface.co is reachable for extra downloads (curl resolve/main URLs).
- 2026-10-16: 4x RTX A6000 (48GB) present but shared — other users' jobs held ~42GB on 3 GPUs and intermittently grabbed the 4th. Approach that worked: vLLM 0.31 (`uv add "vllm>=0.10"`; unpinned `uv add vllm` resolved an ancient 0.4 build), small `gpu_memory_utilization` (~0.11 ≈ 5GB) for ≤1.5B models on the leftover slices, plus a bash wrapper that polls `nvidia-smi` free memory and retries launch. vLLM checks free mem ≥ util×total at startup.
- 2026-10-14 (no GPU then): llama.cpp multi-server CPU fallback worked; `transformers` CPU generation much slower.
- Pitfalls: `pkill -f <pattern>` inside a Bash call whose text contains the pattern kills the calling shell (find PIDs, kill by PID separately). Leftover `nvidia-cudnn-cu12` 8.x from a failed install breaks flashinfer ("Found 2 libcudnn.so.x") — `uv pip uninstall nvidia-cudnn-cu12`. vLLM `prompt_logprobs` materialises full-vocab logits → OOM on small slices; cap `max_num_batched_tokens` (~1024). Don't edit a bash script while a running loop is executing it.
- Label-restricted log-probs in vLLM: `logprobs_mode="processed_logprobs"` + `allowed_token_ids=label_ids` returns log-softmax renormalised over the labels.

Update 2026-10-16 (inter-model-agreement workspace): 4×A6000 present but shared — other neurico sessions keep each GPU at ~6–10 GB free, fluctuating second to second. What worked:
- `uv venv --python 3.12` (default 3.14 breaks vLLM); pyproject needs `requires-python="==3.12.*"` and `[tool.uv] package=false`.
- vLLM 0.31: no bitsandbytes; set `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` (JIT build fails); `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`.
- Use pre-quantized 4-bit AWQ/GPTQ checkpoints (~5.5 GB for 8B): Qwen/*-AWQ, hugging-quants Llama-3.1/gemma-2 AWQ-INT4, tiiuae/Falcon3-7B-Instruct-AWQ, solidrust Mistral AWQ, kaitchup Olmo-3/Phi-3 GPTQ.
- Cap gpu_memory_utilization to ~12.5 GB and retry on startup OOM via a scheduler loop; max_model_len 2560, max_num_seqs 64.
- Gated models in /data/transformers/hub (meta-llama Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, google/gemma-7b-it) have weights but no config/tokenizer → unusable; unsloth mirror of Llama-3.1 is complete. Disk /data is ~100% full.

Update 2026-10-16 (few-shot-ordering workspace, 2nd session): a "Begin research execution" prompt can land on a workspace where a prior session already finished most work (REPORT.md exists, background jobs killed at session end). Check logs/*.status and REPORT first and resume only the interrupted pieces rather than restarting. Monitor `tail -n0 -F` on status files missed an append; poll status files directly instead. Qwen2.5-14B bf16 (~30 GB) won't fit when GPUs have ≤23 GB free.

Update 2026-10-16 (system_prompt_residual_effects workspace): the neurico runner can kill a session at its 6h limit (return_code 143) and relaunch with the same prompt while detached background jobs (e.g. `run_all.sh`) keep running. On start, check for existing planning.md/REPORT.md, `*_PLACEHOLDER` markers, `.neurico/pipeline_*.json`, `*.partial` checkpoints and live PIDs before redoing anything; usually you only need to wait for the jobs and re-run the scoring/analysis.

input.content:
# Planning: Decoding Strategy Sensitivity Across Task Domains

## Motivation & Novelty Assessment

### Why This Research Matters
Benchmark numbers for LLMs are routinely reported under a single, often unstated, decoding
configuration (greedy for leaderboards, T≈0.7 for chat). If a task family's scores or model
*rankings* depend on the decoding strategy, then cross-paper comparisons and leaderboard
conclusions for that family are fragile. Practitioners also need to know which tasks tolerate
sampling (and which sampler to use) without losing accuracy.

### Gap in Existing Work
Note: the resource-finder stage was skipped for this workspace (no `literature_review.md`,
`papers/`, `datasets/`, `code/`), so this is based on prior knowledge. Prior work studies
decoding mostly one task family at a time: Holtzman et al. 2020 (nucleus sampling, open-ended
text), Shi et al. 2024 "A Thorough Examination of Decoding Methods in the Era of LLMs"
(many tasks, but few models and no ranking-stability analysis), Renze & Guven 2024 (temperature
has little effect on MCQA problem solving), Chen et al. 2021 (Codex: temperature vs pass@k),
Nguyen et al. 2024 (min-p sampling). What has not been looked at much is a **single controlled
grid** of models × task domains × decoding strategies × seeds that measures (a) score
sensitivity per domain, (b) how stable the **model rankings** are across strategies
(Kendall τ), and (c) how much each domain varies across seeds.

### Our Novel Contribution
A controlled 11-model × 4-domain × 6-strategy × 3-seed study that tests the five quantitative
claims in the hypothesis, especially the ranking-stability claim (τ>0.9 factual vs τ<0.7
reasoning), which needs many models to test.

### Experiment Justification
- Exp 1 (Factual QA, TriviaQA): tests "factual drops <2% across strategies" and τ>0.9.
- Exp 2 (Reasoning, GSM8K CoT): tests the 5–12% greedy-vs-T=1.0 gap, top-p recovery, τ<0.7.
- Exp 3 (Code, HumanEval pass@1): tests "code shows highest seed variance under sampling".
- Exp 4 (Creative, story writing + LLM-judge proxy): tests "sampling improves creative quality 10–15%".
- Exp 5 (Cross-cutting ranking analysis): Kendall τ between the greedy ranking and each
  strategy's ranking, per domain, with bootstrap CIs.

## Research Question
How sensitive are LLM task scores and model rankings to the decoding strategy, and does that
sensitivity differ between factual QA, multi-step reasoning, code synthesis and creative writing?

## Hypothesis Decomposition
- H1: For every model, |acc(strategy) − acc(greedy)| < 2 points on factual QA (absolute; we also report relative).
- H2: GSM8K accuracy at T=1.0 is 5–12 points below greedy; top-p=0.9 (at T=1.0) recovers most (>50%) of that gap.
- H3: Creative quality (LLM-judge score) under sampling is 10–15% higher (relative) than greedy.
- H4: Kendall τ(greedy ranking, strategy ranking) > 0.9 for factual; < 0.7 for reasoning.
- H5: Std across seeds (per model, per strategy) is largest for code among the four domains.

## Proposed Methodology

### Approach
No API keys are available on this host, so we use **real open-weight instruction-tuned LLMs
served locally with vLLM** (shared RTX A6000 GPUs). 11 models from 7 families:
Qwen2.5-{0.5B,1.5B,3B}-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ, Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507,
Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-AWQ, gemma-2-9b-it-AWQ, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3-AWQ,
Falcon3-7B-Instruct-AWQ, Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct-GPTQ, Olmo-3-7B-Instruct-GPTQ.
The wide spread in model quality is realistic for leaderboards. Small models plus local serving
make a full grid (≈ 11×6×3 runs per task) affordable.

Decoding strategies (6):
1. greedy (T=0)
2. T=0.7 (pure temperature)
3. T=1.0 (pure ancestral sampling)
4. top-p=0.9 at T=1.0
5. top-k=40 at T=1.0
6. min-p=0.1 at T=1.0

Sampled strategies use seeds {0,1,2}. Greedy is run once (deterministic, modulo batch nondeterminism).

### Experimental Steps
1. Data: TriviaQA rc.nocontext validation (n=400 random), GSM8K test (n=400 random),
   HumanEval (all 164), creative: 100 story prompts built from ROCStories first sentences.
2. Generation with vLLM, chat template, zero-shot prompts (in `src/prompts.py`).
3. Scoring: TriviaQA = normalized alias match (EM-or-contains on the short answer);
   GSM8K = last number vs gold; HumanEval = pass@1 by executing the tests in a subprocess with a timeout;
   Creative = Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct (not one of the evaluated models) as judge with a 1–10 rubric
   (creativity, coherence, fluency, engagement; we report the mean), plus distinct-n and
   degeneration rate as auxiliary metrics.
4. Analysis: per (model, domain, strategy) mean over seeds; deltas vs greedy; seed std;
   Kendall τ of model rankings; bootstrap CIs over items; paired tests.

### Baselines
Greedy decoding is the reference condition for every comparison. T=0.7 is the common "chat default".

### Evaluation Metrics
Accuracy / pass@1 / judge score (as described above); Δ vs greedy (absolute points and relative %);
seed std; Kendall τ_b.

### Statistical Analysis Plan
- Per-domain mean Δ vs greedy across models: one-sample t-test and Wilcoxon signed-rank over the 11 models; 95% bootstrap CIs.
- Item-level paired comparisons (greedy vs strategy) pooled across models: McNemar/sign test.
- Kendall τ with 95% CI from bootstrap resampling of items (rankings recomputed for each resample).

# Planning: Decoding Strategy Sensitivity Across Task Domains

## Motivation & Novelty Assessment

### Why This Research Matters
Benchmark numbers for LLMs are routinely reported under a single, often unstated, decoding
configuration (greedy for leaderboards, T≈0.7 for chat). If a task family's scores or model
*rankings* depend on the decoding strategy, then cross-paper comparisons and leaderboard
conclusions for that family are fragile. Practitioners also need to know which tasks tolerate
sampling (and which sampler to use) without losing accuracy.

### Gap in Existing Work
Note: the resource-finder stage was skipped for this workspace (no `literature_review.md`,
`papers/`, `datasets/`, `code/`), so this is based on prior knowledge. Prior work studies
decoding mostly one task family at a time: Holtzman et al. 2020 (nucleus sampling, open-ended
text), Shi et al. 2024 "A Thorough Examination of Decoding Methods in the Era of LLMs"
(many tasks, but few models and no ranking-stability analysis), Renze & Guven 2024 (temperature
has little effect on MCQA problem solving), Chen et al. 2021 (Codex: temperature vs pass@k),
Nguyen et al. 2024 (min-p sampling). What has not been looked at much is a **single controlled
grid** of models × task domains × decoding strategies × seeds that measures (a) score
sensitivity per domain, (b) how stable the **model rankings** are across strategies
(Kendall τ), and (c) how much each domain varies across seeds.

### Our Novel Contribution
A controlled 11-model × 4-domain × 6-strategy × 3-seed study that tests the five quantitative
claims in the hypothesis, especially the ranking-stability claim (τ>0.9 factual vs τ<0.7
reasoning), which needs many models to test.

### Experiment Justification
- Exp 1 (Factual QA, TriviaQA): tests "factual drops <2% across strategies" and τ>0.9.
- Exp 2 (Reasoning, GSM8K CoT): tests the 5–12% greedy-vs-T=1.0 gap, top-p recovery, τ<0.7.
- Exp 3 (Code, HumanEval pass@1): tests "code shows highest seed variance under sampling".
- Exp 4 (Creative, story writing + LLM-judge proxy): tests "sampling improves creative quality 10–15%".
- Exp 5 (Cross-cutting ranking analysis): Kendall τ between the greedy ranking and each
  strategy's ranking, per domain, with bootstrap CIs.

## Research Question
How sensitive are LLM task scores and model rankings to the decoding strategy, and does that
sensitivity differ between factual QA, multi-step reasoning, code synthesis and creative writing?

## Hypothesis Decomposition
- H1: For every model, |acc(strategy) − acc(greedy)| < 2 points on factual QA (absolute; we also report relative).
- H2: GSM8K accuracy at T=1.0 is 5–12 points below greedy; top-p=0.9 (at T=1.0) recovers most (>50%) of that gap.
- H3: Creative quality (LLM-judge score) under sampling is 10–15% higher (relative) than greedy.
- H4: Kendall τ(greedy ranking, strategy ranking) > 0.9 for factual; < 0.7 for reasoning.
- H5: Std across seeds (per model, per strategy) is largest for code among the four domains.

## Proposed Methodology

### Approach
No API keys are available on this host, so we use **real open-weight instruction-tuned LLMs
served locally with vLLM** (shared RTX A6000 GPUs). 11 models from 7 families:
Qwen2.5-{0.5B,1.5B,3B}-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ, Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507,
Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-AWQ, gemma-2-9b-it-AWQ, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3-AWQ,
Falcon3-7B-Instruct-AWQ, Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct-GPTQ, Olmo-3-7B-Instruct-GPTQ.
The wide spread in model quality is realistic for leaderboards. Small models plus local serving
make a full grid (≈ 11×6×3 runs per task) affordable.

Decoding strategies (6):
1. greedy (T=0)
2. T=0.7 (pure temperature)
3. T=1.0 (pure ancestral sampling)
4. top-p=0.9 at T=1.0
5. top-k=40 at T=1.0
6. min-p=0.1 at T=1.0

Sampled strategies use seeds {0,1,2}. Greedy is run once (deterministic, modulo batch nondeterminism).

### Experimental Steps
1. Data: TriviaQA rc.nocontext validation (n=400 random), GSM8K test (n=400 random),
   HumanEval (all 164), creative: 100 story prompts built from ROCStories first sentences.
2. Generation with vLLM, chat template, zero-shot prompts (in `src/prompts.py`).
3. Scoring: TriviaQA = normalized alias match (EM-or-contains on the short answer);
   GSM8K = last number vs gold; HumanEval = pass@1 by executing the tests in a subprocess with a timeout;
   Creative = Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct (not one of the evaluated models) as judge with a 1–10 rubric
   (creativity, coherence, fluency, engagement; we report the mean), plus distinct-n and
   degeneration rate as auxiliary metrics.
4. Analysis: per (model, domain, strategy) mean over seeds; deltas vs greedy; seed std;
   Kendall τ of model rankings; bootstrap CIs over items; paired tests.

### Baselines
Greedy decoding is the reference condition for every comparison. T=0.7 is the common "chat default".

### Evaluation Metrics
Accuracy / pass@1 / judge score (as described above); Δ vs greedy (absolute points and relative %);
seed std; Kendall τ_b.

### Statistical Analysis Plan
- Per-domain mean Δ vs greedy across models: one-sample t-test and Wilcoxon signed-rank over the 11 models; 95% bootstrap CIs.
- Item-level paired comparisons (greedy vs strategy) pooled across models: McNemar/sign test.
- Kendall τ with 95% CI from bootstrap resampling of items (rankings recomputed for each resample).
- Seed variance: compare per-model seed std across domains (Friedman/Wilcoxon), and also
  normalized by the binomial std to control for differing n and base rates.
- α = 0.05, Holm correction within each family of tests.

## Expected Outcomes
Support: factual |Δ|<2; reasoning gap 5–12 with top-p recovery; creative +10–15%; τ_fact>0.9, τ_reason<0.7;
code has the largest seed std. Any domain falling outside these ranges counts as evidence against that sub-claim.

## Timeline and Milestones
Setup 30 min; pipeline test 30 min; generation ≈ 2–3 h (GPU contention dependent); judge 30–60 min;
analysis 45 min; documentation 45 min.

## Potential Challenges
- Shared GPUs: other jobs take memory → small gpu_memory_utilization, retry loop, one model at a time.
- Small models can degenerate at T=1.0 (very long outputs) → max_tokens caps; report degeneration.
- LLM-judge ≠ human judgment → state that it's a proxy; check judge self-consistency; report diversity metrics too.
- Batch nondeterminism in "greedy" → acknowledged.

verdict with CIs, and REPORT.md written.

"""Shared configuration: models, decoding strategies, task prompts, data loading."""
import glob
import json
import os
import random

import pandas as pd

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
HUB = os.environ.get("HF_HUB_CACHE", "/data/transformers/hub")
DATA_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "data")
GEN_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "gen")
SCORE_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "scores")
SEED = 42

# key -> (HF repo id, approx GPU GB needed incl. KV cache)
MODELS = {
    "qwen2.5-0.5b": ("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", 5),
    "qwen2.5-1.5b": ("Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct", 7),
    "qwen2.5-3b": ("Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct", 11),
    "qwen2.5-7b-awq": ("Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ", 11),
    "qwen3-4b-2507": ("Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507", 14),
    "llama3.1-8b-awq": ("hugging-quants/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-AWQ-INT4", 11),
    "gemma2-9b-awq": ("hugging-quants/gemma-2-9b-it-AWQ-INT4", 13),
    "mistral-7b-awq": ("solidrust/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3-AWQ", 10),
    "falcon3-7b-awq": ("tiiuae/Falcon3-7B-Instruct-AWQ", 11),
    "phi3-mini-gptq": ("kaitchup/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct-gptq-4bit", 8),
    "olmo3-7b-gptq": ("kaitchup/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct-gptq-w4a16-g128", 11),
}
JUDGE_MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct"

# Decoding strategies. Sampled strategies are run with SEEDS; greedy once.
STRATEGIES = {
    "greedy": dict(temperature=0.0),
    "t0.7": dict(temperature=0.7),
    "t1.0": dict(temperature=1.0),
    "topp0.9": dict(temperature=1.0, top_p=0.9),
    "topk40": dict(temperature=1.0, top_k=40),
    "minp0.1": dict(temperature=1.0, min_p=0.1),
}
SEEDS = [0, 1, 2]
TASKS = ["factual", "reasoning", "code", "creative"]
MAX_TOKENS = {"factual": 48, "reasoning": 640, "code": 640, "creative": 400}
N_ITEMS = {"factual": 400, "reasoning": 400, "code": 164, "creative": 100}


def runs():
    """All (strategy, seed) pairs."""
    out = [("greedy", 0)]
    for s in STRATEGIES:
        if s != "greedy":
            out += [(s, sd) for sd in SEEDS]
    return out


def _pq(pattern):
    return pd.read_parquet(glob.glob(os.path.join(HUB, pattern))[0])


def build_data():
    """Sample evaluation items once and freeze them in data/*.jsonl."""
    os.makedirs(DATA_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    tq = _pq("datasets--mandarjoshi--trivia_qa/snapshots/*/rc.nocontext/validation-*.parquet")
    idx = rng.sample(range(len(tq)), N_ITEMS["factual"])
    fact = [{"id": tq.iloc[i]["question_id"], "question": tq.iloc[i]["question"],
             "aliases": list(tq.iloc[i]["answer"]["normalized_aliases"]) + [tq.iloc[i]["answer"]["normalized_value"]]}
            for i in idx]
    gs = _pq("datasets--openai--gsm8k/snapshots/*/main/test-*.parquet")
    idx = rng.sample(range(len(gs)), N_ITEMS["reasoning"])
    reas = [{"id": f"gsm8k-{i}", "question": gs.iloc[i]["question"],
             "answer": gs.iloc[i]["answer"].split("####")[-1].strip().replace(",", "")} for i in idx]
    he = _pq("datasets--openai--openai_humaneval/snapshots/*/openai_humaneval/test-*.parquet")
    code = [{"id": r.task_id, "prompt": r.prompt, "test": r.test, "entry_point": r.entry_point}
            for r in he.itertuples()]
    roc = _pq("datasets--hamishivi--ROCStories/snapshots/*/data/test-*.parquet")
    col = "sentence1" if "sentence1" in roc.columns else roc.columns[2]
    idx = rng.sample(range(len(roc)), N_ITEMS["creative"])
    crea = [{"id": f"roc-{i}", "first_sentence": str(roc.iloc[i][col])} for i in idx]
    for name, items in [("factual", fact), ("reasoning", reas), ("code", code), ("creative", crea)]:
        with open(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, f"{name}.jsonl"), "w") as f:
            for it in items:
                f.write(json.dumps(it) + "\n")
        print(name, len(items))


def load_task(task):
    with open(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, f"{task}.jsonl")) as f:
        return [json.loads(l) for l in f]


def make_prompt(task, item):
    """Zero-shot user message for each task (identical across models and strategies)."""
    if task == "factual":
        return ("Answer the following trivia question. Reply with only the answer "
                "(a few words), no explanation.\n\nQuestion: " + item["question"] + "\nAnswer:")
    if task == "reasoning":
        return ("Solve the following math word problem. Think step by step, then write the final "
                "answer on the last line in the form \"The answer is N\".\n\n" + item["question"])
    if task == "code":
        return ("Complete the following Python function. Return the complete function "
                "(signature and body, plus any imports it needs) in a single ```python code block.\n\n"
                "```python\n" + item["prompt"] + "```")
    if task == "creative":
        return ("Write a short, original story of about 150 words that begins with the sentence "
                "below. Make it vivid, surprising and engaging. Output only the story.\n\n"
                "First sentence: " + item["first_sentence"])
    raise ValueError(task)


def gen_path(model, task, strategy, seed):
    return os.path.join(GEN_DIR, model, f"{task}__{strategy}__s{seed}.jsonl")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    build_data()

"""Generate outputs for one model across all tasks x strategies x seeds with vLLM.

Usage: python src/generate.py --model qwen2.5-0.5b --gpu-gb 6
Resumable: (task, strategy, seed) files that already exist are skipped.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from common import MAX_TOKENS, MODELS, STRATEGIES, TASKS, gen_path, load_task, make_prompt, runs  # noqa: E402


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--gpu-gb", type=float, default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--tasks", default=",".join(TASKS))
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=None, help="debug: items per task")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    repo, need_gb = MODELS[args.model]
    gb = args.gpu_gb or need_gb
    todo = [(t, s, sd) for t in args.tasks.split(",") for s, sd in runs()
            if not os.path.exists(gen_path(args.model, t, s, sd))]
    if not todo:
        print("nothing to do"); return

    import torch
    from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

    total = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory / 2**30
    llm = LLM(model=repo, gpu_memory_utilization=gb / total, max_model_len=2048,
              max_num_seqs=128, seed=0, enforce_eager=False, trust_remote_code=True)
    tok = llm.get_tokenizer()

    for task in args.tasks.split(","):
        items = load_task(task)[: args.limit]
        prompts = []
        for it in items:
            msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": make_prompt(task, it)}]
            prompts.append(tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True))
        combos = [(s, sd) for s, sd in runs() if not os.path.exists(gen_path(args.model, task, s, sd))]
        if not combos:
            continue
        # One big batched call covering all (strategy, seed) combos for this task.
        all_prompts, all_sp, keys = [], [], []
        for s, sd in combos:
            for i, p in enumerate(prompts):
                kw = dict(STRATEGIES[s])
                if s != "greedy":
                    kw["seed"] = 100_000 * sd + i  # per-request seed => reproducible regardless of batching
                all_prompts.append(p)
                all_sp.append(SamplingParams(max_tokens=MAX_TOKENS[task], **kw))
                keys.append((s, sd, i))
        t0 = time.time()
        outs = llm.generate(all_prompts, all_sp, use_tqdm=False)
        print(f"[{args.model}] {task}: {len(outs)} gens in {time.time()-t0:.0f}s", flush=True)
        buf = {}
        for (s, sd, i), o in zip(keys, outs):
            c = o.outputs[0]
            buf.setdefault((s, sd), []).append({
                "id": items[i]["id"], "text": c.text, "n_tokens": len(c.token_ids),
                "finish_reason": c.finish_reason})
        for (s, sd), rows in buf.items():
            p = gen_path(args.model, task, s, sd)
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True)
            with open(p + ".tmp", "w") as f:
                for r in rows:
                    f.write(json.dumps(r) + "\n")
            os.replace(p + ".tmp", p)
    print("DONE", args.model)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""GPU scheduler for the shared host: launches one generate.py process per model on whichever
GPU currently has enough free memory, retrying models whose launch fails (e.g. startup OOM
caused by other users' jobs). Logs to logs/gen_<model>.log and logs/run_all.status.
"""
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from common import MODELS, ROOT, TASKS, gen_path, runs  # noqa: E402

MAX_TRIES = 8
LOG = os.path.join(ROOT, "logs")


def free_mem():
    out = subprocess.run(["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=index,memory.free", "--format=csv,noheader,nounits"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    return {int(a): int(b) / 1024 for a, b in (l.split(",") for l in out.strip().splitlines())}


def complete(m):
    return all(os.path.exists(gen_path(m, t, s, sd)) for t in TASKS for s, sd in runs())


def status(msg):
    with open(os.path.join(LOG, "run_all.status"), "a") as f:
        f.write(time.strftime("%H:%M:%S ") + msg + "\n")


def main():
    models = sys.argv[1].split(",") if len(sys.argv) > 1 else list(MODELS)
    pending = [m for m in models if not complete(m)]
    tries = {m: 0 for m in pending}
    running = {}  # model -> (Popen, gpu)
    reserved = {}  # gpu -> GB we expect our running jobs to still be grabbing
    while pending or running:
        for m, (p, g) in list(running.items()):
            if p.poll() is not None:
                del running[m]
                if complete(m):
                    status(f"done {m}")
                else:
                    tries[m] += 1
                    status(f"fail {m} rc={p.returncode} try={tries[m]}")
                    if tries[m] < MAX_TRIES:
                        pending.append(m)
        if pending:
            fm = free_mem()
            m = pending[0]
            need = MODELS[m][1] + 1.5
            gpus = sorted(fm, key=lambda g: -fm[g])
            for g in gpus:
                if fm[g] >= need:
                    env = dict(os.environ, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=str(g))
                    lf = open(os.path.join(LOG, f"gen_{m}.log"), "a")
                    p = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, os.path.join(ROOT, "src", "generate.py"), "--model", m],
                                         env=env, stdout=lf, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
                    running[m] = (p, g)
                    pending.pop(0)
                    status(f"launch {m} on gpu{g} (free {fm[g]:.1f}GB)")
                    time.sleep(75)  # let the process grab its memory before measuring again
                    break
        time.sleep(10)
    status("ALL FINISHED")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import subprocess
import sys
import time

def status(msg):

def main():

    while pending or running:
        for m, (p, g) in list(running.items()):
            if p.poll() is not None:

                if complete(m):

                else:
                    tries[m] += 1
                    status(f"fail {m} rc={p.returncode} try={tries[m]}")
                    if tries[m] < MAX_TRIES:

                    lf = open(os.path.join(LOG, f"gen_{m}.log"), "a")
                    p = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, os.path.join(ROOT, "src", "generate.py"), "--model", m],
                                         env=env, stdout=lf, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
                    running[m] = (p, g)
                    pending.pop(0)
                    status(f"launch {m} on gpu{g} (free {fm[g]:.1f}GB)")
                    time.sleep(75)  # let the process grab its memory before measuring again
                    break
        time.sleep(10)
    status("ALL FINISHED")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""LLM-as-judge proxy for creative quality. A held-out judge model (Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, not
one of the evaluated models) rates each story 1-10 on creativity, coherence, fluency and
engagement, blind to model and decoding strategy. Greedy judge decoding.

Writes results/scores/creative_judge.csv (model, strategy, seed, id, 4 sub-scores, mean).
"""
import argparse
import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys

import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from common import GEN_DIR, JUDGE_MODEL, SCORE_DIR, load_task  # noqa: E402

DIMS = ["creativity", "coherence", "fluency", "engagement"]
JUDGE_PROMPT = """You are an expert creative-writing teacher grading short stories written from a given first sentence.
Rate the story on four criteria, each an integer from 1 (very poor) to 10 (excellent):
- creativity: originality of ideas, surprising but sensible developments, avoids cliches
- coherence: the plot is logically consistent and follows from the first sentence; has a clear arc
- fluency: grammatical, natural, well-formed prose without repetition, gibberish or broken text
- engagement: how interesting and enjoyable it is to read

Be strict and use the full scale. A story that is truncated, degenerate, repetitive or off-task should get low scores.

First sentence: {first}

Story:
\"\"\"
{story}
\"\"\"

Respond with only a JSON object like {{"creativity": x, "coherence": x, "fluency": x, "engagement": x}}."""


def parse(text):
    out = {}
    for d in DIMS:
        m = re.search(r'"?' + d + r'"?\s*:\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)', text, flags=re.I)
        out[d] = min(10.0, max(1.0, float(m.group(1)))) if m else float("nan")
    return out


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--gpu-gb", type=float, default=36)
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    import torch
    from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

    firsts = {it["id"]: it["first_sentence"] for it in load_task("creative")}
    rows, prompts = [], []
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(GEN_DIR, "*", "creative__*.jsonl"))):
        model = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(f))
        _, strategy, seed = os.path.basename(f)[:-6].split("__")
        for line in open(f):
            g = json.loads(line)
            rows.append(dict(model=model, strategy=strategy, seed=int(seed[1:]), id=g["id"]))
            # Cap story length fed to the judge (outputs are already capped at 400 tokens).
            prompts.append(JUDGE_PROMPT.format(first=firsts[g["id"]], story=g["text"].strip()[:3000]))
    rows, prompts = rows[: args.limit], prompts[: args.limit]
    total = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory / 2**30
    llm = LLM(model=JUDGE_MODEL, gpu_memory_utilization=args.gpu_gb / total, max_model_len=2048,
              max_num_seqs=128, seed=0)
    tok = llm.get_tokenizer()
    chats = [tok.apply_chat_template([{"role": "user", "content": p}], tokenize=False,
                                     add_generation_prompt=True) for p in prompts]
    outs = llm.generate(chats, SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=60))
    for r, o in zip(rows, outs):
        r.update(parse(o.outputs[0].text))
        r["judge_raw"] = o.outputs[0].text
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df["judge_mean"] = df[DIMS].mean(axis=1)
    os.makedirs(SCORE_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    df.to_csv(os.path.join(SCORE_DIR, "creative_judge.csv" if args.limit is None else "creative_judge_test.csv"), index=False)
    print("parse failures:", df[DIMS].isna().any(axis=1).sum())
    print(df.groupby("strategy")["judge_mean"].mean().round(3))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Statistical analysis of decoding-strategy sensitivity. Reads results/scores/*.csv and writes
results/analysis/*.csv|json and figures/*.png.

Scores: factual/reasoning/code are 0/1 per item (shown as % points); creative is the mean
LLM-judge rating on a 1-10 scale.
"""
import json
import os
import sys

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402
import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
from scipy import stats  # noqa: E402

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from common import ROOT, SCORE_DIR, STRATEGIES, TASKS  # noqa: E402

OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "analysis")
FIG = os.path.join(ROOT, "figures")
SAMPLED = [s for s in STRATEGIES if s != "greedy"]
N_BOOT = 1000
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)


def load():
    df = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(SCORE_DIR, "item_scores.csv"))
    df["id"] = df["id"].astype(str)
    jp = os.path.join(SCORE_DIR, "creative_judge.csv")
    if os.path.exists(jp):
        j = pd.read_csv(jp)[["model", "strategy", "seed", "id", "judge_mean"]]
        j["id"] = j["id"].astype(str)
        df = df.merge(j, on=["model", "strategy", "seed", "id"], how="left")
        cm = df.task == "creative"
        df.loc[cm, "score"] = df.loc[cm, "judge_mean"]
    df = df.dropna(subset=["score"])
    # Keep only models that have the complete grid for every task (balanced design).
    cnt = df.groupby(["model", "task"]).apply(lambda g: g[["strategy", "seed"]].drop_duplicates().shape[0])
    full = cnt.unstack().dropna()
    full = full[(full == 16).all(axis=1)].index
    return df[df.model.isin(full)]


def scale(task):
    return 1.0 if task == "creative" else 100.0


def model_means(d):
    """model x strategy mean score (averaged over items, then over seeds)."""
    per_seed = d.groupby(["model", "strategy", "seed"])["score"].mean()
    return per_seed.groupby(["model", "strategy"]).mean().unstack()[list(STRATEGIES)]


def kendall_vs_greedy(mm):
    return {s: stats.kendalltau(mm["greedy"], mm[s]).statistic for s in SAMPLED}


def main():
    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(FIG, exist_ok=True)
    df = load()
    models = sorted(df.model.unique())
    print("models:", len(models), models)
    summary, per_model_rows, tau_rows, seed_rows, tests = {}, [], [], [], []

    for task in TASKS:
        d = df[df.task == task]
        if d.empty:
            continue
        k = scale(task)
        mm = model_means(d) * k
        mm.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, f"model_means_{task}.csv"))
        delta = mm.sub(mm["greedy"], axis=0)
        rel = delta.div(mm["greedy"], axis=0) * 100
        for m in mm.index:
            for s in STRATEGIES:
                per_model_rows.append(dict(task=task, model=m, strategy=s, score=mm.loc[m, s],
                                           delta=delta.loc[m, s], rel_delta_pct=rel.loc[m, s]))
        # Across-model tests of delta vs greedy (Wilcoxon signed-rank; also t-test).
        for s in SAMPLED:
            w = stats.wilcoxon(delta[s]) if (delta[s] != 0).any() else None
            t = stats.ttest_1samp(delta[s], 0)
            tests.append(dict(task=task, strategy=s, mean_delta=delta[s].mean(), sd_delta=delta[s].std(),
                              min_delta=delta[s].min(), max_delta=delta[s].max(),
                              max_abs_delta=delta[s].abs().max(),
                              mean_rel_pct=rel[s].mean(), median_rel_pct=rel[s].median(),
                              t_p=t.pvalue, wilcoxon_p=(w.pvalue if w else 1.0)))

        # Kendall tau with item-bootstrap CI: resample items, recompute model means & rankings.
        piv = d.pivot_table(index="id", columns=["model", "strategy", "seed"], values="score")
        ids = piv.index.values
        base = kendall_vs_greedy(mm)
        boots = {s: [] for s in SAMPLED}
        mean_pair_boot = []
        for _ in range(N_BOOT):
            samp = piv.loc[rng.choice(ids, len(ids), replace=True)].mean()
            bm = samp.groupby(level=["model", "strategy"]).mean().unstack()[list(STRATEGIES)]
            for s, v in kendall_vs_greedy(bm).items():
                boots[s].append(v)
        # Seed-to-seed ranking stability within a sampled strategy (seed i vs seed j).
        ps = d.groupby(["model", "strategy", "seed"])["score"].mean().unstack()
        for s in STRATEGIES:
            lo, hi = (np.nanpercentile(boots[s], [2.5, 97.5]) if s in boots else (np.nan, np.nan))
            within = []
            if s != "greedy":
                x = ps.xs(s, level="strategy")
                within = [stats.kendalltau(x[a], x[b]).statistic for a, b in [(0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 2)]]
            tau_rows.append(dict(task=task, strategy=s, tau_vs_greedy=base.get(s, 1.0), ci_lo=lo, ci_hi=hi,
                                 frac_boot_gt_0_9=(np.mean(np.array(boots[s]) > 0.9) if s in boots else np.nan),
                                 tau_seed_vs_seed=np.mean(within) if within else np.nan))
        # Mean over all strategy pairs (alternative stability summary).
        pair_taus = [stats.kendalltau(mm[a], mm[b]).statistic
                     for i, a in enumerate(STRATEGIES) for b in list(STRATEGIES)[i + 1:]]
        # Seed variability: std over seeds of the run-level score, per model & sampled strategy.
        for s in SAMPLED:
            x = ps.xs(s, level="strategy") * k
            sub = d[d.strategy == s]
            # Per-item flip rate: fraction of items whose 0/1 outcome is not identical across seeds.
            itm = sub.pivot_table(index=["model", "id"], columns="seed", values="score")
            if task == "creative":
                flip = itm.std(axis=1).groupby(level="model").mean()  # item-level judge-score std
            else:
                flip = (itm.nunique(axis=1) > 1).groupby(level="model").mean() * 100
            for m in x.index:
                p = mm.loc[m, s] / k
                n = d.id.nunique()
                binom_se = np.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n) * k if task != "creative" else np.nan
                seed_rows.append(dict(task=task, model=m, strategy=s, seed_std=x.loc[m].std(ddof=1),
                                      seed_range=x.loc[m].max() - x.loc[m].min(),
                                      seed_cv_pct=x.loc[m].std(ddof=1) / max(1e-9, x.loc[m].mean()) * 100,
                                      item_flip=flip.loc[m], binom_se=binom_se))
        summary[task] = dict(
            n_items=int(d.id.nunique()), n_models=len(mm),
            mean_by_strategy=mm.mean().round(3).to_dict(),
            mean_delta_vs_greedy=delta.mean().round(3).to_dict(),
            mean_rel_delta_pct=rel.mean().round(2).to_dict(),
            max_abs_delta_any_model_any_strategy=float(delta[SAMPLED].abs().max().max()),
            tau_vs_greedy={k_: round(v, 3) for k_, v in base.items()},

            gap = mm["greedy"] - mm["t1.0"]
            rec = (mm["topp0.9"] - mm["t1.0"]) / gap.where(gap.abs() > 1e-9)
            pooled_rec = (mm["topp0.9"].mean() - mm["t1.0"].mean()) / (mm["greedy"].mean() - mm["t1.0"].mean())
            summary[task]["greedy_minus_t1"] = gap.round(2).to_dict()
            summary[task]["topp_recovery_fraction_per_model"] = rec.round(3).to_dict()
            summary[task]["topp_recovery_fraction_pooled"] = float(pooled_rec)
            summary[task]["minp_recovery_fraction_pooled"] = float(
                (mm["minp0.1"].mean() - mm["t1.0"].mean()) / (mm["greedy"].mean() - mm["t1.0"].mean()))

    pm = pd.DataFrame(per_model_rows); pm.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "per_model_scores.csv"), index=False)
    tt = pd.DataFrame(tests)
    # Holm correction across all (task, strategy) Wilcoxon tests.
    order = np.argsort(tt.wilcoxon_p.values); m_ = len(order); adj = np.empty(m_); run = 0
    for r, i in enumerate(order):

    sd = pd.DataFrame(seed_rows); sd.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "seed_variability.csv"), index=False)

    # H5: compare seed variability across domains.
    seedsum = sd.groupby("task")[["seed_std", "seed_range", "seed_cv_pct", "item_flip", "binom_se"]].mean()
    seedsum["std_over_binomSE"] = (sd.seed_std / sd.binom_se).groupby(sd.task).mean()
    seedsum.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "seed_variability_by_task.csv"))
    acc_tasks = [t for t in ["factual", "reasoning", "code"] if t in sd.task.unique()]
    h5 = {}
    for metric in ["seed_std", "item_flip"]:
        # Per (model, strategy) cell, compare code vs each other accuracy task (paired Wilcoxon).
        piv = sd.pivot_table(index=["model", "strategy"], columns="task", values=metric)
        for t in acc_tasks:

                    code_mean=float(piv["code"].mean()), other_mean=float(piv[t].mean()),
                    wilcoxon_p=float(stats.wilcoxon(piv["code"], piv[t]).pvalue))
    summary["seed_variability_by_task"] = seedsum.round(3).to_dict()
    summary["h5_tests"] = h5
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "summary.json"), "w") as f:
        json.dump(summary, f, indent=2, default=float)
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=1, default=float)[:6000])
    print(tt.round(4).to_string())
    print(tau.round(3).to_string())
    print(seedsum.round(3).to_string())
    make_figures(pm, tau, sd)


def make_figures(pm, tau, sd):
    tasks = [t for t in TASKS if t in pm.task.unique()]
    strat = list(STRATEGIES)
    colors = ["#1f3b73", "#4878cf", "#6acc65", "#d65f5f", "#b47cc7", "#c4ad66"]
    # Fig 1: mean delta vs greedy (relative %) per task x strategy, with per-model points.
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(tasks), figsize=(4.2 * len(tasks), 4), sharey=False)
    for ax, t in zip(np.atleast_1d(axes), tasks):
        x = pm[(pm.task == t) & (pm.strategy != "greedy")]
        for i, s in enumerate(SAMPLED):
            v = x[x.strategy == s].delta.values
            ax.bar(i, v.mean(), color=colors[i + 1], alpha=0.8)
            ax.scatter(np.full(len(v), i) + rng.uniform(-0.18, 0.18, len(v)), v, s=10, color="k", zorder=3)
        ax.axhline(0, color="grey", lw=0.8)
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(SAMPLED))); ax.set_xticklabels(SAMPLED, rotation=35)
        ax.set_title(t)
        ax.set_ylabel("Δ vs greedy (judge pts, 1–10)" if t == "creative" else "Δ vs greedy (acc. pts)")
    fig.suptitle("Score change vs greedy decoding (bar = mean over models, dots = individual models)")
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "delta_vs_greedy.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 2: per-model score by strategy (lines).
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(tasks), figsize=(4.2 * len(tasks), 4))
    for ax, t in zip(np.atleast_1d(axes), tasks):
        x = pm[pm.task == t].pivot(index="model", columns="strategy", values="score")[strat]
        for m in x.index:
            ax.plot(range(len(strat)), x.loc[m].values, marker="o", ms=3, lw=1, label=m)
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(strat))); ax.set_xticklabels(strat, rotation=35); ax.set_title(t)
    np.atleast_1d(axes)[-1].legend(fontsize=6, loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1, 0.5))
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "per_model_by_strategy.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 3: Kendall tau vs greedy with bootstrap CIs.
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
    w = 0.8 / len(SAMPLED)
    for i, s in enumerate(SAMPLED):
        x = tau[(tau.strategy == s)].set_index("task").loc[tasks]
        pos = np.arange(len(tasks)) + (i - len(SAMPLED) / 2 + 0.5) * w
        ax.bar(pos, x.tau_vs_greedy, w, color=colors[i + 1], label=s,
               yerr=[x.tau_vs_greedy - x.ci_lo, x.ci_hi - x.tau_vs_greedy], capsize=2)
    ax.axhline(0.9, ls="--", color="k", lw=0.8); ax.axhline(0.7, ls=":", color="k", lw=0.8)
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(tasks))); ax.set_xticklabels(tasks); ax.set_ylabel("Kendall τ vs greedy ranking")
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.05); ax.legend(fontsize=7, ncol=5, loc="lower center")
    ax.set_title("Model-ranking stability (95% item-bootstrap CI); dashed=0.9, dotted=0.7")
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "kendall_tau.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 4: seed variability per task.
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4))
    data = [sd[sd.task == t].seed_std.values for t in tasks]
    axes[0].boxplot(data, labels=tasks); axes[0].set_ylabel("std over 3 seeds (score units)")
    axes[0].set_title("Run-level seed std (per model×strategy)")
    data = [sd[sd.task == t].item_flip.values for t in tasks if t != "creative"]
    axes[1].boxplot(data, labels=[t for t in tasks if t != "creative"])
    axes[1].set_ylabel("% items with outcome differing across seeds"); axes[1].set_title("Item-level seed instability")
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "seed_variability.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Statistical analysis of decoding-strategy sensitivity. Reads results/scores/*.csv and writes
results/analysis/*.csv|json and figures/*.png.

Scores: factual/reasoning/code are 0/1 per item (shown as % points); creative is the mean
LLM-judge rating on a 1-10 scale.
"""
import json
import os
import sys

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402
import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
from scipy import stats  # noqa: E402

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from common import ROOT, SCORE_DIR, STRATEGIES, TASKS  # noqa: E402

OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "analysis")
FIG = os.path.join(ROOT, "figures")
SAMPLED = [s for s in STRATEGIES if s != "greedy"]
N_BOOT = 1000
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)


def load():
    df = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(SCORE_DIR, "item_scores.csv"))
    df["id"] = df["id"].astype(str)
    jp = os.path.join(SCORE_DIR, "creative_judge.csv")
    if os.path.exists(jp):
        j = pd.read_csv(jp)[["model", "strategy", "seed", "id", "judge_mean"]]
        j["id"] = j["id"].astype(str)
        df = df.merge(j, on=["model", "strategy", "seed", "id"], how="left")
        cm = df.task == "creative"
        df.loc[cm, "score"] = df.loc[cm, "judge_mean"]
    df = df.dropna(subset=["score"])
    # Keep only models that have the complete grid for every task (balanced design).
    cnt = df.groupby(["model", "task"]).apply(lambda g: g[["strategy", "seed"]].drop_duplicates().shape[0])
    full = cnt.unstack().dropna()
    full = full[(full == 16).all(axis=1)].index
    return df[df.model.isin(full)]


def scale(task):
    return 1.0 if task == "creative" else 100.0


def model_means(d):
    """model x strategy mean score (averaged over items, then over seeds)."""
    per_seed = d.groupby(["model", "strategy", "seed"])["score"].mean()
    return per_seed.groupby(["model", "strategy"]).mean().unstack()[list(STRATEGIES)]


def kendall_vs_greedy(mm):
    return {s: stats.kendalltau(mm["greedy"], mm[s]).statistic for s in SAMPLED}


def main():
    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(FIG, exist_ok=True)
    df = load()
    models = sorted(df.model.unique())
    print("models:", len(models), models)
    summary, per_model_rows, tau_rows, seed_rows, tests = {}, [], [], [], []

    for task in TASKS:
        d = df[df.task == task]
        if d.empty:
            continue
        k = scale(task)
        mm = model_means(d) * k
        mm.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, f"model_means_{task}.csv"))
        delta = mm.sub(mm["greedy"], axis=0)
        rel = delta.div(mm["greedy"], axis=0) * 100
        for m in mm.index:
            for s in STRATEGIES:
                per_model_rows.append(dict(task=task, model=m, strategy=s, score=mm.loc[m, s],
                                           delta=delta.loc[m, s], rel_delta_pct=rel.loc[m, s]))
        # Across-model tests of delta vs greedy (Wilcoxon signed-rank; also t-test).
        for s in SAMPLED:
            w = stats.wilcoxon(delta[s]) if (delta[s] != 0).any() else None
            t = stats.ttest_1samp(delta[s], 0)
            tests.append(dict(task=task, strategy=s, mean_delta=delta[s].mean(), sd_delta=delta[s].std(),
                              min_delta=delta[s].min(), max_delta=delta[s].max(),
                              max_abs_delta=delta[s].abs().max(),
                              mean_rel_pct=rel[s].mean(), median_rel_pct=rel[s].median(),
                              t_p=t.pvalue, wilcoxon_p=(w.pvalue if w else 1.0)))

        # Kendall tau with item-bootstrap CI: resample items, recompute model means & rankings.
        piv = d.pivot_table(index="id", columns=["model", "strategy", "seed"], values="score")
        ids = piv.index.values
        base = kendall_vs_greedy(mm)
        boots = {s: [] for s in SAMPLED}
        mean_pair_boot = []
        for _ in range(N_BOOT):
            samp = piv.loc[rng.choice(ids, len(ids), replace=True)].mean()
            bm = samp.groupby(level=["model", "strategy"]).mean().unstack()[list(STRATEGIES)]
            for s, v in kendall_vs_greedy(bm).items():
                boots[s].append(v)
        # Seed-to-seed ranking stability within a sampled strategy (seed i vs seed j).
        ps = d.groupby(["model", "strategy", "seed"])["score"].mean().unstack()
        for s in STRATEGIES:
            lo, hi = (np.nanpercentile(boots[s], [2.5, 97.5]) if s in boots else (np.nan, np.nan))
            within = []
            if s != "greedy":
                x = ps.xs(s, level="strategy")
                within = [stats.kendalltau(x[a], x[b]).statistic for a, b in [(0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 2)]]
            tau_rows.append(dict(task=task, strategy=s, tau_vs_greedy=base.get(s, 1.0), ci_lo=lo, ci_hi=hi,
                                 frac_boot_gt_0_9=(np.mean(np.array(boots[s]) > 0.9) if s in boots else np.nan),
                                 tau_seed_vs_seed=np.mean(within) if within else np.nan))
        # Mean over all strategy pairs (alternative stability summary).
        pair_taus = [stats.kendalltau(mm[a], mm[b]).statistic
                     for i, a in enumerate(STRATEGIES) for b in list(STRATEGIES)[i + 1:]]
        # Seed variability: std over seeds of the run-level score, per model & sampled strategy.
        for s in SAMPLED:
            x = ps.xs(s, level="strategy") * k
            sub = d[d.strategy == s]
            # Per-item flip rate: fraction of items whose 0/1 outcome is not identical across seeds.
            itm = sub.pivot_table(index=["model", "id"], columns="seed", values="score")
            if task == "creative":
                flip = itm.std(axis=1).groupby(level="model").mean()  # item-level judge-score std
            else:
                flip = (itm.nunique(axis=1) > 1).groupby(level="model").mean() * 100
            for m in x.index:
                p = mm.loc[m, s] / k
                n = d.id.nunique()
                binom_se = np.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n) * k if task != "creative" else np.nan
                seed_rows.append(dict(task=task, model=m, strategy=s, seed_std=x.loc[m].std(ddof=1),
                                      seed_range=x.loc[m].max() - x.loc[m].min(),
                                      seed_cv_pct=x.loc[m].std(ddof=1) / max(1e-9, x.loc[m].mean()) * 100,
                                      item_flip=flip.loc[m], binom_se=binom_se))
        summary[task] = dict(
            n_items=int(d.id.nunique()), n_models=len(mm),
            mean_by_strategy=mm.mean().round(3).to_dict(),
            mean_delta_vs_greedy=delta.mean().round(3).to_dict(),
            mean_rel_delta_pct=rel.mean().round(2).to_dict(),
            max_abs_delta_any_model_any_strategy=float(delta[SAMPLED].abs().max().max()),
            tau_vs_greedy={k_: round(v, 3) for k_, v in base.items()},
            mean_pairwise_tau_all_strategies=float(np.mean(pair_taus)),
            ranking_greedy=list(mm["greedy"].sort_values(ascending=False).index),
        )
        if task == "reasoning":
            gap = mm["greedy"] - mm["t1.0"]
            rec = (mm["topp0.9"] - mm["t1.0"]) / gap.where(gap.abs() > 1e-9)
            pooled_rec = (mm["topp0.9"].mean() - mm["t1.0"].mean()) / (mm["greedy"].mean() - mm["t1.0"].mean())
            summary[task]["greedy_minus_t1"] = gap.round(2).to_dict()
            summary[task]["topp_recovery_fraction_per_model"] = rec.round(3).to_dict()
            summary[task]["topp_recovery_fraction_pooled"] = float(pooled_rec)
            summary[task]["minp_recovery_fraction_pooled"] = float(
                (mm["minp0.1"].mean() - mm["t1.0"].mean()) / (mm["greedy"].mean() - mm["t1.0"].mean()))

    pm = pd.DataFrame(per_model_rows); pm.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "per_model_scores.csv"), index=False)
    tt = pd.DataFrame(tests)
    # Holm correction across all (task, strategy) Wilcoxon tests.
    order = np.argsort(tt.wilcoxon_p.values); m_ = len(order); adj = np.empty(m_); run = 0
    for r, i in enumerate(order):
        run = max(run, min(1, (m_ - r) * tt.wilcoxon_p.values[i])); adj[i] = run
    tt["wilcoxon_p_holm"] = adj
    tt.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "delta_tests.csv"), index=False)
    tau = pd.DataFrame(tau_rows); tau.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "kendall_tau.csv"), index=False)
    sd = pd.DataFrame(seed_rows); sd.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "seed_variability.csv"), index=False)

    # H5: compare seed variability across domains.
    seedsum = sd.groupby("task")[["seed_std", "seed_range", "seed_cv_pct", "item_flip", "binom_se"]].mean()
    seedsum["std_over_binomSE"] = (sd.seed_std / sd.binom_se).groupby(sd.task).mean()
    seedsum.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "seed_variability_by_task.csv"))
    acc_tasks = [t for t in ["factual", "reasoning", "code"] if t in sd.task.unique()]
    h5 = {}
    for metric in ["seed_std", "item_flip"]:
        # Per (model, strategy) cell, compare code vs each other accuracy task (paired Wilcoxon).
        piv = sd.pivot_table(index=["model", "strategy"], columns="task", values=metric)
        for t in acc_tasks:
            if t != "code" and "code" in piv:
                h5[f"{metric}: code vs {t}"] = dict(
                    code_mean=float(piv["code"].mean()), other_mean=float(piv[t].mean()),
                    wilcoxon_p=float(stats.wilcoxon(piv["code"], piv[t]).pvalue))
    summary["seed_variability_by_task"] = seedsum.round(3).to_dict()
    summary["h5_tests"] = h5
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "summary.json"), "w") as f:
        json.dump(summary, f, indent=2, default=float)
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=1, default=float)[:6000])
    print(tt.round(4).to_string())
    print(tau.round(3).to_string())
    print(seedsum.round(3).to_string())
    make_figures(pm, tau, sd)


def make_figures(pm, tau, sd):
    tasks = [t for t in TASKS if t in pm.task.unique()]
    strat = list(STRATEGIES)
    colors = ["#1f3b73", "#4878cf", "#6acc65", "#d65f5f", "#b47cc7", "#c4ad66"]
    # Fig 1: mean delta vs greedy (relative %) per task x strategy, with per-model points.
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(tasks), figsize=(4.2 * len(tasks), 4), sharey=False)
    for ax, t in zip(np.atleast_1d(axes), tasks):
        x = pm[(pm.task == t) & (pm.strategy != "greedy")]
        for i, s in enumerate(SAMPLED):
            v = x[x.strategy == s].delta.values
            ax.bar(i, v.mean(), color=colors[i + 1], alpha=0.8)
            ax.scatter(np.full(len(v), i) + rng.uniform(-0.18, 0.18, len(v)), v, s=10, color="k", zorder=3)
        ax.axhline(0, color="grey", lw=0.8)
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(SAMPLED))); ax.set_xticklabels(SAMPLED, rotation=35)
        ax.set_title(t)
        ax.set_ylabel("Δ vs greedy (judge pts, 1–10)" if t == "creative" else "Δ vs greedy (acc. pts)")
    fig.suptitle("Score change vs greedy decoding (bar = mean over models, dots = individual models)")
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "delta_vs_greedy.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 2: per-model score by strategy (lines).
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(tasks), figsize=(4.2 * len(tasks), 4))
    for ax, t in zip(np.atleast_1d(axes), tasks):
        x = pm[pm.task == t].pivot(index="model", columns="strategy", values="score")[strat]
        for m in x.index:
            ax.plot(range(len(strat)), x.loc[m].values, marker="o", ms=3, lw=1, label=m)
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(strat))); ax.set_xticklabels(strat, rotation=35); ax.set_title(t)
    np.atleast_1d(axes)[-1].legend(fontsize=6, loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1, 0.5))
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "per_model_by_strategy.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 3: Kendall tau vs greedy with bootstrap CIs.
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
    w = 0.8 / len(SAMPLED)
    for i, s in enumerate(SAMPLED):
        x = tau[(tau.strategy == s)].set_index("task").loc[tasks]
        pos = np.arange(len(tasks)) + (i - len(SAMPLED) / 2 + 0.5) * w
        ax.bar(pos, x.tau_vs_greedy, w, color=colors[i + 1], label=s,

    ax.axhline(0.9, ls="--", color="k", lw=0.8); ax.axhline(0.7, ls=":", color="k", lw=0.8)
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(tasks))); ax.set_xticklabels(tasks); ax.set_ylabel("Kendall τ vs greedy ranking")
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.05); ax.legend(fontsize=7, ncol=5, loc="lower center")
    ax.set_title("Model-ranking stability (95% item-bootstrap CI); dashed=0.9, dotted=0.7")
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "kendall_tau.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 4: seed variability per task.

    data = [sd[sd.task == t].seed_std.values for t in tasks]
    axes[0].boxplot(data, labels=tasks); axes[0].set_ylabel("std over 3 seeds (score units)")

    data = [sd[sd.task == t].item_flip.values for t in tasks if t != "creative"]

"""Statistical analysis of decoding-strategy sensitivity. Reads results/scores/*.csv and writes
results/analysis/*.csv|json and figures/*.png.

Scores: factual/reasoning/code are 0/1 per item (shown as % points); creative is the mean
LLM-judge rating on a 1-10 scale.
"""
import json
import os
import sys

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402
import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
from scipy import stats  # noqa: E402

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from common import ROOT, SCORE_DIR, STRATEGIES, TASKS  # noqa: E402

OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "analysis")
FIG = os.path.join(ROOT, "figures")
SAMPLED = [s for s in STRATEGIES if s != "greedy"]
N_BOOT = 1000
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)


def load():
    df = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(SCORE_DIR, "item_scores.csv"))
    df["id"] = df["id"].astype(str)
    jp = os.path.join(SCORE_DIR, "creative_judge.csv")
    if os.path.exists(jp):
        j = pd.read_csv(jp)[["model", "strategy", "seed", "id", "judge_mean"]]
        j["id"] = j["id"].astype(str)
        df = df.merge(j, on=["model", "strategy", "seed", "id"], how="left")
        cm = df.task == "creative"
        df.loc[cm, "score"] = df.loc[cm, "judge_mean"]
    df = df.dropna(subset=["score"])
    # Keep only models that have the complete grid for every task (balanced design).
    cnt = df.groupby(["model", "task"]).apply(lambda g: g[["strategy", "seed"]].drop_duplicates().shape[0])
    full = cnt.unstack().dropna()
    full = full[(full == 16).all(axis=1)].index
    return df[df.model.isin(full)]


def scale(task):
    return 1.0 if task == "creative" else 100.0


def model_means(d):
    """model x strategy mean score (averaged over items, then over seeds)."""
    per_seed = d.groupby(["model", "strategy", "seed"])["score"].mean()
    return per_seed.groupby(["model", "strategy"]).mean().unstack()[list(STRATEGIES)]


def kendall_vs_greedy(mm):
    return {s: stats.kendalltau(mm["greedy"], mm[s]).statistic for s in SAMPLED}


def main():
    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(FIG, exist_ok=True)
    df = load()
    models = sorted(df.model.unique())
    print("models:", len(models), models)
    summary, per_model_rows, tau_rows, seed_rows, tests = {}, [], [], [], []

    for task in TASKS:
        d = df[df.task == task]
        if d.empty:
            continue
        k = scale(task)
        mm = model_means(d) * k
        mm.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, f"model_means_{task}.csv"))
        delta = mm.sub(mm["greedy"], axis=0)
        rel = delta.div(mm["greedy"], axis=0) * 100
        for m in mm.index:
            for s in STRATEGIES:
                per_model_rows.append(dict(task=task, model=m, strategy=s, score=mm.loc[m, s],
                                           delta=delta.loc[m, s], rel_delta_pct=rel.loc[m, s]))
        # Across-model tests of delta vs greedy (Wilcoxon signed-rank; also t-test).
        for s in SAMPLED:
            w = stats.wilcoxon(delta[s]) if (delta[s] != 0).any() else None
            t = stats.ttest_1samp(delta[s], 0)
            tests.append(dict(task=task, strategy=s, mean_delta=delta[s].mean(), sd_delta=delta[s].std(),
                              min_delta=delta[s].min(), max_delta=delta[s].max(),
                              max_abs_delta=delta[s].abs().max(),
                              mean_rel_pct=rel[s].mean(), median_rel_pct=rel[s].median(),
                              t_p=t.pvalue, wilcoxon_p=(w.pvalue if w else 1.0)))

        # Kendall tau with item-bootstrap CI: resample items, recompute model means & rankings.
        piv = d.pivot_table(index="id", columns=["model", "strategy", "seed"], values="score")
        ids = piv.index.values
        base = kendall_vs_greedy(mm)
        boots = {s: [] for s in SAMPLED}
        mean_pair_boot = []
        for _ in range(N_BOOT):
            samp = piv.loc[rng.choice(ids, len(ids), replace=True)].mean()
            bm = samp.groupby(level=["model", "strategy"]).mean().unstack()[list(STRATEGIES)]
            for s, v in kendall_vs_greedy(bm).items():
                boots[s].append(v)
        # Seed-to-seed ranking stability within a sampled strategy (seed i vs seed j).
        ps = d.groupby(["model", "strategy", "seed"])["score"].mean().unstack()
        for s in STRATEGIES:
            lo, hi = (np.nanpercentile(boots[s], [2.5, 97.5]) if s in boots else (np.nan, np.nan))
            within = []
            if s != "greedy":
                x = ps.xs(s, level="strategy")
                within = [stats.kendalltau(x[a], x[b]).statistic for a, b in [(0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 2)]]
            tau_rows.append(dict(task=task, strategy=s, tau_vs_greedy=base.get(s, 1.0), ci_lo=lo, ci_hi=hi,
                                 frac_boot_gt_0_9=(np.mean(np.array(boots[s]) > 0.9) if s in boots else np.nan),
                                 tau_seed_vs_seed=np.mean(within) if within else np.nan))
        # Mean over all strategy pairs (alternative stability summary).
        pair_taus = [stats.kendalltau(mm[a], mm[b]).statistic
                     for i, a in enumerate(STRATEGIES) for b in list(STRATEGIES)[i + 1:]]
        # Seed variability: std over seeds of the run-level score, per model & sampled strategy.
        for s in SAMPLED:
            x = ps.xs(s, level="strategy") * k
            sub = d[d.strategy == s]
            # Per-item flip rate: fraction of items whose 0/1 outcome is not identical across seeds.
            itm = sub.pivot_table(index=["model", "id"], columns="seed", values="score")
            if task == "creative":
                flip = itm.std(axis=1).groupby(level="model").mean()  # item-level judge-score std
            else:
                flip = (itm.nunique(axis=1) > 1).groupby(level="model").mean() * 100
            for m in x.index:
                p = mm.loc[m, s] / k
                n = d.id.nunique()
                binom_se = np.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n) * k if task != "creative" else np.nan
                seed_rows.append(dict(task=task, model=m, strategy=s, seed_std=x.loc[m].std(ddof=1),
                                      seed_range=x.loc[m].max() - x.loc[m].min(),
                                      seed_cv_pct=x.loc[m].std(ddof=1) / max(1e-9, x.loc[m].mean()) * 100,
                                      item_flip=flip.loc[m], binom_se=binom_se))
        summary[task] = dict(
            n_items=int(d.id.nunique()), n_models=len(mm),
            mean_by_strategy=mm.mean().round(3).to_dict(),
            mean_delta_vs_greedy=delta.mean().round(3).to_dict(),
            mean_rel_delta_pct=rel.mean().round(2).to_dict(),
            max_abs_delta_any_model_any_strategy=float(delta[SAMPLED].abs().max().max()),
            tau_vs_greedy={k_: round(v, 3) for k_, v in base.items()},
            mean_pairwise_tau_all_strategies=float(np.mean(pair_taus)),
            ranking_greedy=list(mm["greedy"].sort_values(ascending=False).index),
        )
        if task == "reasoning":
            gap = mm["greedy"] - mm["t1.0"]
            rec = (mm["topp0.9"] - mm["t1.0"]) / gap.where(gap.abs() > 1e-9)
            pooled_rec = (mm["topp0.9"].mean() - mm["t1.0"].mean()) / (mm["greedy"].mean() - mm["t1.0"].mean())
            summary[task]["greedy_minus_t1"] = gap.round(2).to_dict()
            summary[task]["topp_recovery_fraction_per_model"] = rec.round(3).to_dict()
            summary[task]["topp_recovery_fraction_pooled"] = float(pooled_rec)
            summary[task]["minp_recovery_fraction_pooled"] = float(
                (mm["minp0.1"].mean() - mm["t1.0"].mean()) / (mm["greedy"].mean() - mm["t1.0"].mean()))

    pm = pd.DataFrame(per_model_rows); pm.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "per_model_scores.csv"), index=False)
    tt = pd.DataFrame(tests)
    # Holm correction across all (task, strategy) Wilcoxon tests.
    order = np.argsort(tt.wilcoxon_p.values); m_ = len(order); adj = np.empty(m_); run = 0
    for r, i in enumerate(order):
        run = max(run, min(1, (m_ - r) * tt.wilcoxon_p.values[i])); adj[i] = run
    tt["wilcoxon_p_holm"] = adj
    tt.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "delta_tests.csv"), index=False)
    tau = pd.DataFrame(tau_rows); tau.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "kendall_tau.csv"), index=False)
    sd = pd.DataFrame(seed_rows); sd.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "seed_variability.csv"), index=False)

    # H5: compare seed variability across domains.
    seedsum = sd.groupby("task")[["seed_std", "seed_range", "seed_cv_pct", "item_flip", "binom_se"]].mean()
    seedsum["std_over_binomSE"] = (sd.seed_std / sd.binom_se).groupby(sd.task).mean()
    seedsum.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "seed_variability_by_task.csv"))
    acc_tasks = [t for t in ["factual", "reasoning", "code"] if t in sd.task.unique()]
    h5 = {}
    for metric in ["seed_std", "item_flip"]:
        # Per (model, strategy) cell, compare code vs each other accuracy task (paired Wilcoxon).
        piv = sd.pivot_table(index=["model", "strategy"], columns="task", values=metric)
        for t in acc_tasks:
            if t != "code" and "code" in piv:
                h5[f"{metric}: code vs {t}"] = dict(
                    code_mean=float(piv["code"].mean()), other_mean=float(piv[t].mean()),
                    wilcoxon_p=float(stats.wilcoxon(piv["code"], piv[t]).pvalue))
    summary["seed_variability_by_task"] = seedsum.round(3).to_dict()
    summary["h5_tests"] = h5
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "summary.json"), "w") as f:
        json.dump(summary, f, indent=2, default=float)
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=1, default=float)[:6000])
    print(tt.round(4).to_string())
    print(tau.round(3).to_string())
    print(seedsum.round(3).to_string())
    make_figures(pm, tau, sd)


def make_figures(pm, tau, sd):
    tasks = [t for t in TASKS if t in pm.task.unique()]
    strat = list(STRATEGIES)
    colors = ["#1f3b73", "#4878cf", "#6acc65", "#d65f5f", "#b47cc7", "#c4ad66"]
    # Fig 1: mean delta vs greedy (relative %) per task x strategy, with per-model points.
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(tasks), figsize=(4.2 * len(tasks), 4), sharey=False)
    for ax, t in zip(np.atleast_1d(axes), tasks):
        x = pm[(pm.task == t) & (pm.strategy != "greedy")]
        for i, s in enumerate(SAMPLED):
            v = x[x.strategy == s].delta.values
            ax.bar(i, v.mean(), color=colors[i + 1], alpha=0.8)
            ax.scatter(np.full(len(v), i) + rng.uniform(-0.18, 0.18, len(v)), v, s=10, color="k", zorder=3)
        ax.axhline(0, color="grey", lw=0.8)
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(SAMPLED))); ax.set_xticklabels(SAMPLED, rotation=35)
        ax.set_title(t)
        ax.set_ylabel("Δ vs greedy (judge pts, 1–10)" if t == "creative" else "Δ vs greedy (acc. pts)")
    fig.suptitle("Score change vs greedy decoding (bar = mean over models, dots = individual models)")
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "delta_vs_greedy.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 2: per-model score by strategy (lines).
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(tasks), figsize=(4.2 * len(tasks), 4))
    for ax, t in zip(np.atleast_1d(axes), tasks):
        x = pm[pm.task == t].pivot(index="model", columns="strategy", values="score")[strat]
        for m in x.index:
            ax.plot(range(len(strat)), x.loc[m].values, marker="o", ms=3, lw=1, label=m)
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(strat))); ax.set_xticklabels(strat, rotation=35); ax.set_title(t)
    np.atleast_1d(axes)[-1].legend(fontsize=6, loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1, 0.5))
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "per_model_by_strategy.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 3: Kendall tau vs greedy with bootstrap CIs.
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
    w = 0.8 / len(SAMPLED)
    for i, s in enumerate(SAMPLED):
        x = tau[(tau.strategy == s)].set_index("task").loc[tasks]
        pos = np.arange(len(tasks)) + (i - len(SAMPLED) / 2 + 0.5) * w
        ax.bar(pos, x.tau_vs_greedy, w, color=colors[i + 1], label=s,
               yerr=[x.tau_vs_greedy - x.ci_lo, x.ci_hi - x.tau_vs_greedy], capsize=2)
    ax.axhline(0.9, ls="--", color="k", lw=0.8); ax.axhline(0.7, ls=":", color="k", lw=0.8)
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(tasks))); ax.set_xticklabels(tasks); ax.set_ylabel("Kendall τ vs greedy ranking")
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.05); ax.legend(fontsize=7, ncol=5, loc="lower center")
    ax.set_title("Model-ranking stability (95% item-bootstrap CI); dashed=0.9, dotted=0.7")
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "kendall_tau.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 4: seed variability per task.
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4))
    data = [sd[sd.task == t].seed_std.values for t in tasks]
    axes[0].boxplot(data, labels=tasks); axes[0].set_ylabel("std over 3 seeds (score units)")
    axes[0].set_title("Run-level seed std (per model×strategy)")
    data = [sd[sd.task == t].item_flip.values for t in tasks if t != "creative"]
    axes[1].boxplot(data, labels=[t for t in tasks if t != "creative"])
    axes[1].set_ylabel("% items with outcome differing across seeds"); axes[1].set_title("Item-level seed instability")
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "seed_variability.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Generate outputs for one model across all tasks x strategies x seeds with vLLM.

Usage: python src/generate.py --model qwen2.5-0.5b --gpu-gb 6
Resumable: (task, strategy, seed) files that already exist are skipped.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from common import MAX_TOKENS, MODELS, STRATEGIES, TASKS, gen_path, load_task, make_prompt, runs  # noqa: E402


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--gpu-gb", type=float, default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--tasks", default=",".join(TASKS))
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=None, help="debug: items per task")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    repo, need_gb = MODELS[args.model]
    gb = args.gpu_gb or need_gb
    todo = [(t, s, sd) for t in args.tasks.split(",") for s, sd in runs()
            if not os.path.exists(gen_path(args.model, t, s, sd))]
    if not todo:
        print("nothing to do"); return

    import torch
    from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

    total = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory / 2**30
    llm = LLM(model=repo, gpu_memory_utilization=gb / total, max_model_len=2048,
              max_num_seqs=128, max_num_batched_tokens=4096, seed=0, trust_remote_code=False)
    tok = llm.get_tokenizer()

    for task in args.tasks.split(","):
        items = load_task(task)[: args.limit]
        prompts = []
        for it in items:
            msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": make_prompt(task, it)}]
            prompts.append(tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True))
        combos = [(s, sd) for s, sd in runs() if not os.path.exists(gen_path(args.model, task, s, sd))]
        if not combos:
            continue
        # One big batched call covering all (strategy, seed) combos for this task.
        all_prompts, all_sp, keys = [], [], []
        for s, sd in combos:
            for i, p in enumerate(prompts):
                kw = dict(STRATEGIES[s])
                if s != "greedy":
                    kw["seed"] = 100_000 * sd + i  # per-request seed => reproducible regardless of batching
                all_prompts.append(p)
                all_sp.append(SamplingParams(max_tokens=MAX_TOKENS[task], **kw))
                keys.append((s, sd, i))
        t0 = time.time()
        outs = llm.generate(all_prompts, all_sp, use_tqdm=False)
        print(f"[{args.model}] {task}: {len(outs)} gens in {time.time()-t0:.0f}s", flush=True)
        buf = {}
        for (s, sd, i), o in zip(keys, outs):
            c = o.outputs[0]
            buf.setdefault((s, sd), []).append({
                "id": items[i]["id"], "text": c.text, "n_tokens": len(c.token_ids),
                "finish_reason": c.finish_reason})
        for (s, sd), rows in buf.items():
            p = gen_path(args.model, task, s, sd)
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True)
            with open(p + ".tmp", "w") as f:
                for r in rows:
                    f.write(json.dumps(r) + "\n")
            os.replace(p + ".tmp", p)
    print("DONE", args.model)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/bin/bash
# Wait until some GPU has >= 10.5 GB free, then run the (incremental) creative judge there.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
source .venv/bin/activate
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 HF_HOME=/data/transformers TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
for attempt in $(seq 1 200); do

    echo "$(date +%T) judge attempt $attempt on gpu$g" >> logs/judge.status
    if CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$g python src/judge.py --gpu-gb 9.2 >> logs/judge.log 2>&1; then
      echo "$(date +%T) judge DONE" >> logs/judge.status; exit 0
    fi
    echo "$(date +%T) judge failed" >> logs/judge.status
  fi
  sleep 20
done
EOF
chmod +x src/launch_judge.sh; setsid nohup src/launch_judge.sh > /dev/null 2>&1 & echo ok

def creative_extras(df):
    """Creative: judge sub-scores, lexical diversity, length and truncation per strategy."""
    jp = os.path.join(SCORE_DIR, "creative_judge.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(jp):
        return
    j = pd.read_csv(jp)
    models = set(df[df.task == "creative"].model)
    j = j[j.model.isin(models)]
    dims = ["creativity", "coherence", "fluency", "engagement", "judge_mean"]
    c = df[df.task == "creative"]
    # Average within model first, then across models (each model weighted equally).
    sub = j.groupby(["model", "strategy"])[dims].mean().groupby("strategy").mean()
    lex = c.groupby(["model", "strategy"])[["distinct2", "n_words", "truncated"]].mean().groupby("strategy").mean()
    out = sub.join(lex).loc[list(STRATEGIES)]
    out["judge_parse_fail_pct"] = j.groupby("strategy")[dims[:4]].apply(lambda x: x.isna().any(axis=1).mean() * 100)
    out.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "creative_breakdown.csv"))
    print(out.round(3).to_string())
    # Per-model relative change of judge score vs greedy, best sampled strategy per model.
    pm = j.groupby(["model", "strategy"]).judge_mean.mean().unstack()
    rel = pm.sub(pm["greedy"], axis=0).div(pm["greedy"], axis=0) * 100
    rel.round(2).to_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "creative_rel_change_per_model.csv"))
    print(rel.round(2).to_string())
